before: Haplotype analysis suggested a common founder for this variant, leading to the recommendation that c.3791G>A (p.R1264H) be considered for inclusion in Ashkenazi carrier screening panels [1].

Among 53 Israeli patients with dihydrolipoamide dehydrogenase deficiency, the c.685G>T (p.G229C) variant in homozygous form was the most common, observed predominantly among patients of Ashkenazi-Jewish descent and accounting for 45.3% of patients [2].
